What the numbers say

In this revision 83 option-selling candidates across 18 underlyings passed the report's filters, all of them short puts. Expiries run from 1 to 73 days out with a median of 10 days; 30 of the 83 expire within seven days and 6 are more than 21 days out.

The highest composite score is 74.5 for the AMD 440 put expiring 2026-11-04 (1 day): premium $3.55, strike 9.9% below the share price, model probability of expiring out of the money 84.3%. Its displayed annualized yield of 294.5% multiplies a 1-day premium out to a full year, which is why the score discounts yields from contracts shorter than 30 days.

Implied volatility among the listed contracts is highest for AMD (156.3%), MRVL (90.2%), SPCX (77.8%) and lowest for COST (25.5%). High implied volatility is what makes a premium large; it is the market's price for a wide expected range, so the richest premiums sit on the names the market expects to move most.

Of the 27 underlyings with a quote, 14 were up and 13 down when the report was generated; the median move was +0.28%. Rising share prices move existing short puts further out of the money and shrink the premium available on new ones.

Against the previous session in this archive (2026-11-02), listed candidates went from 89 to 83 and the median time to expiry went from 11 to 10 days.

Backtest reference

The report carries a fixed reference backtest covering 2026-03-26 to 2026-04-22: 2,149 simulated option-selling trades with a 83.3% win rate and a profit factor of 0.70. A profit factor below 1 means total losses exceeded total gains even though most trades won. That is the characteristic risk of selling premium: many small wins and a few large losses. The window is short and does not include the session on this page; it is a description of that period, not an estimate of future results.
